overview: Saudi Arabia covers most of the Arabian Peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Riyadh. The kingdom was founded in 1932. It is the birthplace of Islam and home to its two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, which millions of pilgrims visit every year. Saudi Arabia has some of the largest oil reserves in the world.

geography.text: Most of Saudi Arabia is desert, including the Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter, the largest continuous sand desert in the world. Mountains run along the west, parallel to the Red Sea coast, and the east faces the Persian Gulf. Saudi Arabia is the largest country in the world with no permanent rivers.

history.text: Islam began in Mecca in the early 600s with the Prophet Muhammad, and the region has been its spiritual heart ever since. In the 1700s the Al Saud family allied with the religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab. Abdulaziz Ibn Saud united most of Arabia and founded the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932, and oil, found in 1938, transformed the country.

events.title: The Hijra
events.text: Muhammad and his followers move from Mecca to Medina; the Islamic calendar begins.

events.title: Saud–Wahhab alliance
events.text: An alliance forms the first Saudi state.

events.title: Kingdom founded
events.text: Ibn Saud proclaims the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

events.title: Oil found
events.text: Commercial oil is discovered at Dammam.

government.text: Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy ruled by the Al Saud family. The King is head of state and government, and there is no elected parliament. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman runs much of the government day to day. Since 2017 the country has relaxed some social rules, such as allowing women to drive, while cracking down on critics.

economy.text: Saudi Arabia has some of the world's largest oil reserves and is one of the biggest oil exporters. Saudi Aramco is one of the most valuable companies in the world. Under its Vision 2030 plan, it is spending heavily on tourism, sport, entertainment and giant projects such as the NEOM city.

culture.text: Saudi Arabia is home to Islam's two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, and millions of Muslims make the Hajj pilgrimage every year. Coffee and dates are central to hospitality. AlUla, with tombs carved by the Nabataeans, has opened to tourists.

items.title: The Hajj
items.text: The pilgrimage to Mecca, a duty for Muslims who are able.

items.title: Hegra
items.text: Nabataean tombs at AlUla, Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO site.

items.title: Arabic coffee
items.text: Served with dates as a sign of welcome, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Saudi Arabia beat eventual champions Argentina at the 2022 World Cup and will host the 2034 World Cup. Its league has signed stars such as Cristiano Ronaldo.

items.text: Beat Argentina 2–1 at the World Cup.
Saudi Arabia will host the men's World Cup.
